text.p: These are some of the leading stories in the official Vietnamese press on Friday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
-- National Assembly Chairman Nong Duc Manh called on the courts and inspectorate to be more courageous in rooting out and punishing corruption and smuggling cases to restore respect for the law.
-- The government has tightened controls on the use and distribution of material used in the maufacture of narcotics.

-- Foreign carmakers in Vietnam said cooperation should be promoted to implement the government's programme of "Vietnamising" cars produced in Vietnam. Deputy Industry Minister Nguyen Xuan Chuan denied that the government had turned down a Hyundai-initiated project to assemble cars in Vietnam.
-- Vietnam's urban-area unemployment rate fell to 5.8 percent last year from 6.08 percent in 1994.

-- Vietnam's biggest corruption trial began on Thurdsay. Twenty people were brought to court, including Pham Huy Phuoc, who was charged with embezzling and causing losses of $26.6 million for the state.
-- The Government has issued a decree to increase pension subsidies and minimum wages for civil servants.
-- Vietnam has condemned U.S radio "Free Asia" for interfering in the internal affairs of other nations.
